t: Of the funds appropriated for the fiscal year 1981 to carry out part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, other than funds appropriated for the Economic Support Fund, $2,000,000 shall be used to carry out this title.

fable.w: This section only earmarks a portion of fiscal year 1981 Foreign Assistance Act funds to carry out the title. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: $2,000,000 shall be used to carry out this title.

opus.w: This provision only sets aside $2,000,000 of fiscal year 1981 Foreign Assistance Act funds to carry out the title. It does not involve consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies or any outside party in a federal decision. Mentioning another statute as the source of the money does not create any process for outsiders to take part.
opus.b: The section only earmarks money. It sets aside $2,000,000 of fiscal year 1981 Foreign Assistance Act funds for "this title." It names no outside party, consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue. The one possible trap is the reference to another Act, but that is just a funding source and involves no process.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause that allocates a specific sum of money for a defined purpose. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or other forms of participation as defined. The mere mention of 'Foreign Assistance' does not imply a participatory process within the text of this specific section.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds appropriated for the fiscal year 1981 to carry out part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, other than funds appropriated for the Economic Support Fund, $2,000,000 shall be used to carry out this title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "Foreign Assistance," they inherently involve coordination with foreign governments or NGOs. However, the text itself is purely an appropriation clause specifying the amount and source of funds. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties. It simply states how much money is available for a specific purpose.
